reported.title: 16-bit int accumulator overflows in ADC window sum
reported.description: The rolling-window accumulator `sum` is declared `int` (line 11), which is 16-bit on ATmega328P, but it accumulates up to WINDOW=50 raw samples of up to 1023 (lines 54-55), reaching ~51150 and overflowing past 32767. The overflowed negative sum is divided by n (line 59) and converted to a percent (line 60), so the firmware printed -148.6 % at 3.00 s while the injected input was 489.08 to 495.15 % (off by 637.7 %), and -140.3 % at 500.0 % input. The accumulator must be a wider type (e.g. long/uint32_t). Firmware printed -148.6 % at 3.00 s while the injected input was 489.08 to 495.15 %: off by 637.7 % (tolerance ±3). 6 of 6 values were wrong.

reported.title: Button handling with delay(30) stalls the periodic pct stream
reported.description: Every loop iteration that reads D5 LOW calls forceSampleNote() and then delay(30) (lines 65-69) with no debounce, so contact chatter and rapid presses repeatedly block the loop and stretch the time between window fills and STATUS_MS checks. The measured pct: gaps reached 1246 ms, 1337 ms and 2523 ms against the 1000 ± 150 ms requirement, and the first line appeared only at 1.72 s. The blocking delay and lack of debounce must be removed so the periodic cadence is preserved. Expected /^pct: / every 1000 ± 150 ms; 4 of 7 intervals were out of tolerance, worst gap 1246 ms.

exposing_checks.behaviour: serial values for 'pct: (-?[0-9.]+)' match the stimulus (tolerance 3.0) (percent correct)

judge_input.spec:
- Concentration probe on A4 at 10 mV per percent; force-sample button on D5 (pull-up, active LOW).
- Average a rolling window of ADC samples and print `pct: <value>` about once per second.
- Printed percent must stay within ±3.0 of the injected probe value.
- Lines matching `pct: ` must appear every 1000 ms ±150 ms.
- Holding D5 LOW may emit a `blend force last=<n>` note without replacing the periodic `pct:` stream.
- Every 1000 ms also print `blend batches=<n>` for batch accounting.
